vignette: John is a 46-year-old European man who works as a graphic designer. He has been married to his wife, Sarah, for over two decades and together they have raised their now-adult children. John’s life changed dramatically one evening after work when he witnessed a violent confrontation between a local gang member and law enforcement officers in front of his home. That night, while walking back from the train station with his briefcase in hand, John heard commotion coming from across the street. He turned to see an officer attempting to detain a man who was clearly agitated and wielding what appeared to be a knife. The situation escalated quickly; the suspect lunged at the officer, and in self-defense, the officer fired multiple shots, hitting the man several times. John stood frozen, watching as the suspect fell to the ground, blood pooling around him. Officers immediately swarmed the scene, securing it with caution tape and sirens blaring. Since that night, John’s life has been irrevocably altered. He constantly feels on edge, his mind replaying the violent confrontation in vivid detail whenever he closes his eyes or tries to relax. The sound of sirens can trigger intense panic attacks where he finds himself gasping for air and sweating profusely. His graphic design work often involves creating visuals that evoke strong emotions, which has become particularly challenging since the incident. At home, John’s relationship with Sarah has been strained. He becomes easily agitated by small disturbances—like a car alarm in the middle of the night—and these reactions have left her feeling as though she is walking on eggshells around him. Recently, he has started avoiding going out after dark, a significant change for someone who used to enjoy evening strolls with Sarah and occasional dinners at their favorite local restaurant. John’s work performance has also suffered. The constant distraction of intrusive thoughts about the confrontation makes it difficult for him to concentrate on his projects. He often finds himself staring blankly at his computer screen, unable to focus or generate creative ideas. This self-imposed isolation from social interactions at work and in his personal life has left him feeling more disconnected than ever. One evening, John decided to revisit the site where he witnessed the shooting after a particularly distressing daydream about it during lunch. Standing on the corner, he felt an overwhelming sense of dread and nausea rising up inside him. The street was quiet now, but his mind conjured up the chaos that had unfolded just weeks earlier. He realized how much the event had altered his perception of safety and security. In an effort to cope with these intense feelings, John has started taking long walks during the day, hoping to clear his head and regain some semblance of normalcy. However, even on these walks, he often finds himself hyper-vigilant, scanning the environment for any signs of danger or reminders of that fateful night. John’s world now feels like a constant balancing act between trying to maintain his daily life and navigating the overwhelming memories and emotions that continue to plague him. Despite his efforts to move forward, the experience remains a deeply embedded part of his present reality, coloring how he interacts with the world around him.
